title: Introduce SDK compatibility shim and unified stream cancellation surface
author: Mariana Silva
release_notes: Adds a compatibility shim that unifies small behavioral differences across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs for auth retries and stream cancellation. Bumps TS/Go/Py SDKs, improves ergonomics for cancelable streams, and documents migration steps.
description: Context: Multiple teams reported subtle incompatibilities between SDKs around streaming cancellation, retry semantics when auth refreshes occur, and slightly different ergonomics for consumer code (async generators in Python, async iterators in TS, and channel semantics in Go). This caused intermittent integration flakes in customers using cross-language clients and in internal e2e tests. Motivation: Provide a small, low-risk compatibility shim and a single documented cancellation surface across SDKs so application code can implement predictable shutdown and auth-retry behavior. Scope: - Introduces an SDK-level compatibility shim (SdkCompat) that normalizes: 1) stream cancellation semantics (graceful close vs immediate abort), 2) auth retry hooks and TTL refresh handoff, 3) backoff profiles naming and mapping across languages. - Adds a cancelable stream handle API for each SDK (py: CancelableAsyncGenerator, ts: CancelableAsyncIterator, go: CancelableStreamHandle) that shares behavioral guarantees. - Small, backwards-compatible ergonomics wrappers for Python/TS/Go to reduce boilerplate for common patterns (prefetch+reauth, graceful drain, and forced abort). - Adds cross-language e2e parity tests and sample snippets in quickstarts. Design highlights: - SdkCompat is implemented as a minimal shim exported behind feature-flag SDK_COMPAT_2026_02; default is enabled for new releases and can be toggled for canary customers. - Cancellation semantics: calling cancel() will attempt graceful drain with a short grace window (default 250ms) before issuing an immediate abort. Grace window is configurable per-client. - Auth retry handoff: when an in-flight streaming request receives an auth-refresh event, the SDK will attempt one in-band retry with preserved ordering guarantees; if retry fails due to transient auth errors, the stream surface will emit a RecoverableAuthError and keep the consumer-facing iterator open so app-level retry policies can resume. - Backoff mapping: the shim maps our internal retry profiles to language-native presets (e.g., retry_fast -> RetryPreset.FAST) and ensures identical jitter and base-delay semantics across SDKs. Testing: - Unit tests added for each shim path (py/ts/go). - Cross-language e2e harness: new scenario that opens streams, forces token refresh mid-stream, cancels from client-side, and asserts expected events. - Performance: measured extra overhead on microbenchmarks ~0.6% median per-token latency when shim enabled; added toggle to disable shim for critical perf runs. Migration and rollout: - Docs: quick migration guide under docs/sdk/compat-shim.md with example snippets for Python, TypeScript, and Go. - Version bumps: py 3.12.0, ts 1.27.0, go 1.9.0. - Release plan: enable shim by default behind feature flag in this release; promote to mandatory after 4 weeks internal canary. Backwards compatibility: behavior preserved for existing sync-only flows; streaming apps may opt into stricter abort semantics via client config. Checklist: - [x] Implementation across Python/TS/Go - [x] Unit + e2e tests - [x] Docs and migration examples - [x] CI green (lint/build/test) - [x] Version bumps and changelogs included

review_comments: Ethan Monroe: Can we reduce the default grace window from 250ms to 150ms? Some internal low-latency apps still saw visible hiccups. Reply (Mariana Silva): We measured 150ms and saw a small uptick in aborted in-flight chunks for slower networks; 250ms is a compromise. Added a client opt to override graceWindowMs so teams can tune.

Kai Nakamura: The RecoverableAuthError surface seems leaky — how should callers detect permanent failures? Reply (Mariana Silva): Added an isPermanent flag and documented RetryPolicy.shouldCloseStream in the migration guide. Also added a deterministic example showing exponential fallback to alternative model endpoints.

Sofia Ahmed: Please run canary suite against Dedicated infra for auth storm scenarios. Reply (Mariana Silva): Ran two Dedicated canary runs (region-us-west-2) and attached logs to the PR; no regressions.
CI Bot: Lint failure in ts shim.ts (unused import). Reply (Mariana Silva): Fixed in commit ff12aa3. CI rerun passed.

notes_for_release_manager: Feature-flagged rollout. Default enabled for this tagged release. For customers with ultra-low-latency SLAs, support will coordinate temporary opt-out. Ensure quickstart snippets are linked from the SDK changelog.
migration_examples: Python: with client.configure(grace_window_ms=150, enable_compat=True): async for chunk in client.stream(...): if should_cancel: await client.cancel_stream(handle)
TypeScript: const handle = client.openStream(...); handle.cancel({graceWindowMs:150}); for await (const chunk of handle) { if (shouldCancel) { await handle.cancel() } }
Go: h, err := client.OpenStream(ctx, opts); go func(){ time.Sleep(150*time.Millisecond); h.Cancel() }(); for ev := range h.Recv() { ... }
